name: 1. Tiroler Holzmuseum Auffach
kurzbeschreibung: The 1st Tyrolean Wood Museum in Auffach in the Wildschönau showcases over 3,000 fascinating wood carvings, antique tools, and curiosities by artist Hubert Salcher.
beschreibung:
Overview

The renowned 1st Tyrolean Wood Museum (1. Tiroler Holzmuseum) is housed within a listed, two-hundred-year-old sun-bleached alpine farmhouse in the idyllic hamlet of Auffach in the Wildschönau high valley. Founded, curated, and operated with tireless passion by master woodcarver and artist Hubert Salcher, this extraordinary private museum displays more than three thousand artfully arranged exhibits. The museum serves as a heartfelt homage to timber, a sustainable natural material that has decisively shaped daily life, architecture, and survival in the rugged alpine mountains for centuries.

Route & Requirements

A self-guided tour through the rustic timber farmhouse spans two floors containing more than thirty labyrinthine rooms, workshops, and traditional parlors. Notable exhibits include intricate hand-carved sculptures, historical wooden clogs, antique folk toys, traditional tools of coopers, wheelwrights, and carpenters, and curious wooden artifacts gathered from around the world. Fragrant Swiss stone pine wood and creaking floorboards create an unmatched cozy alpine atmosphere. During live demonstrations, visitors can watch the master carver practice his craft and gain insights into traditional carving techniques. The historic timber structure has limited wheelchair accessibility; comfortable flat footwear is recommended.

Visit & Arrival

The museum opens from mid-May through late October: Wednesday to Friday from 10:00 to 17:00 (also on Tuesdays during July and August; group tours available year-round by appointment). Admission is approx. €8.00 for adults and €4.00 for children; Wildschönau Card holders receive discounted admission at the desk. Public transit: take the train to Wörgl station and transfer to the regional Postbus line 4064 directly to Auffach; the Auffach Holzmuseum stop is just two minutes away on foot. Motorists drive via the A12 motorway (exit Wörgl Ost) into the Wildschönau valley; free parking is available right outside the entrance.

Tips

In the rustic on-site museum shop, visitors can purchase hand-carved gifts, fragrant pine pillows, bowls, and authentic original carvings created by the artist. Pair your visit with a scenic gondola ride on the Schatzbergbahn Auffach up into the alpine hiking area, or stop at a traditional mountain inn to taste regional Tyrolean Krautkrapfen pastries.
